nodes.question: How does carrying a load affect tire deformation in tractors?
nodes.answer: Carrying a load causes the tire to deform, increasing the contact patch area until the load is supported without further deformation, which is critical for performance and safety.
nodes.paragraph: Depending on theage and capabilities of the tractor, the key sources of data are: In-cab, real-time monitoring of engine performance, and Learning the speci C signals that indicate the limits of engine speed reduction possible for a given gearing and load (engine sound can be misleading, so black smoke coming from the exhaust is also a good indicator, as islack of engine speed response to an increase in throttle setting). Optimizing Tire Inflation Pressure Tires should always be in ated to the manufacturer S rec- ommended in ation pressure for a given load, speed, and surface conditions (ground carrying capacity and slope). When carrying a load over a rm or hard surface the tirede ects, causing an increase of the contact patch area until the load can be supported without further deformation of the tire. A loaded tire is de ected near the contact patchand is continuously exed as it rolls along. For most agricultural tires, the maximum de ection is limited to about 18 20% of the section height, to prevent damagein icted on the carcass (the casing of the tire).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Sustainable agriculture energy|Electric tractors and farm machinery_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the status of electric-powered and hybrid tractors in terms of commercialization?
nodes.answer: Electric-powered tractors are near to commercialization or are already commercially available, while hybrid electric-driven tractors present advantages in energy use efficiency and functionalities.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract The energy use and emissions from direct fossil fuel combustion on-farms to power farm machinery was criticallyreviewed. Approximately, 15% of agricultural production costs on-farm are energy-related. A potential solution to more sustainable energy use is a shift toward biofuels from renewable resources. The reduction of greenhouse gas emissions through the substitution of diesel oil with biodiesel depends on the feedstock, the inter-esteri cation process, the storageperiod, and ambient conditions. In modern tractors, increased fuel use ef ciency (or reduced fuel consumption) has been achieved by power/load matching and the use of variable transmission. Engine management systems that are capable of continuously communicating with the engine and transmission to make appropriate adjustments based on inputs receivedfrom the tractor allow for quick and precise responses to changing conditions. As a result, maximum ef ciency and productivity can be obtained from the tractor operating similarly to the traditional gear-up and throttle-back methods of a pro cient operator. The future for autonomous tractors is promising, though not new. Electric-powered tractors are near tocommercialization or are already commercially available. Hybrid electric driven tractors present some advantages in terms of increased energy use ef ciency and functionalities.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What potential does small lightweight robotic equipment have in farming?
nodes.answer: Small lightweight robotic equipment can potentially perform functions currently undertaken by heavy equipment with high fuel consumption, without compromising field operating capacity.
nodes.paragraph: Increased ef ciency can lead to a reduction in diesel fuel con- sumption and hence, a concurrent decrease in CO 2emission. Where the local electricity supply has a low-carbon emission factor, this can also result in signi cant emission reductions. Small light-weight robotic equipment can potentially perform functions currently undertaken by tractor-drawn and other heavy equipment with high-fuel consumption, provided eld operating capacity was not compromised. However, the size and weight limitations inherent in current harvesting andtransport technology mean that soil compaction will still be a problem with robotic units. The robotic operation of medium- scale equipment within a precision-controlled traf C farming environment should offer more feasible and energy-ef cient alternatives. nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Sustainable agriculture energy|Electric tractors and farm machinery_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What types of energy use are covered in the analysis of farm machinery?
nodes.answer: The analysis primarily focuses on direct fossil fuel combustion on farms to power farm machinery, specifically tractors.
nodes.paragraph: A review of past and recent research was undertaken to identify ways of reducing energy-related costs and envi- ronmental impacts associated with the operation of farmmachinery and on-farm energy use. Indirect energy use (e.g., use of fossil fuels in manufacturing inputs such as animal feed or fertilizer) is brie y covered in this analysis, however, other on-farm energy uses such as for heating orventilation of buildings and other sources of GHG emis- sions (e.g., biogenic methane from ruminant livestock, nitrous oxide emissions arising from animal manure andnitrogen fertilizer use) are not discussed. The work re ects, primarily, an Australian perspective, but it draws from relevant evidence reported elsewhere. The highly mecha- nized Australian agricultural systems resemble large-holder (arable) enterprises found in other parts of the world, par-ticularly the USA, Canada, Brazil, and Argentina [ 64]. Hence, the analysis presented here is also relevant to those systems. Therefore, a key focus of this review was tocritically discuss energy use and emissions from direct fossil fuel combustion on farms to power farm machinery, speci cally tractors.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Sustainable agriculture energy|Electric tractors and farm machinery_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is one method suggested for cutting fuel costs on mechanized farms?
nodes.answer: One method for cutting fuel costs is operating machinery more efficiently, including maintaining clean fuel and air filters, which can save approximately 380 liters of diesel fuel annually.
nodes.paragraph: Most mechanized farms depend on diesel fuel to run tractors, farm vehicles, harvesters, and other farm equipment. Fossilfuels are the main energy costs for arable farm operations representing up to 75% of the total energy spent on modern industrial-scale farms, depending on the cropping system[96]. Small-scale and subsistence farms in developing countries have traditionally relied on animal traction and human labor, including for transport of products to mar-kets, and hence have been less dependent on fossil fuel inputs. However, recent developments in mechanization for smallholder systems and mechanization adoption hasincreased the demand for fuel in those systems [ 10]. Cut- ting fuel costs can be relatively simple, starting with operating machinery in a smarter manner; for example, bycorrectly setting up and maintaining vehicles and equip- ment, and developing a fuel management plan. As an example, US research has shown that the basic practice ofmaintaining clean fuel and air Iters can save around 380 L (*100 US gallons) of diesel fuel annually. Buying more fuel-ef cient vehicles can also result in signi cant fuelsavings, which may be considered as part of the machinery replacement program [ 41].

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Sustainable agriculture energy|Electric tractors and farm machinery_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What types of farming operations may not require full tractor power?
nodes.answer: Many field operations such as light tillage, planting, mechanical weed control, spraying, and hay-raking may not require full tractor power.
nodes.paragraph: On-farm energy use and energy useef ciency in small-holder agriculture settings were con- sidered to be outside the scope of this work and as such they merit a separate analysis. Hence, it is recommendedthat this work is expanded by undertaking a similar review analysis relevant to small landholder farming systems. Techniques for Optimizing Tractor Fuel Consumption Adaptive Driving: Gear-up and Throttle-back Gear-up and throttle-back (GUTB) is a fuel-saving practice that has been popular around the world since the fuel crisis of the mid-1970s. The GUTB technique can be imple-mented to save fuel when drawbar loads are light ( \75% of rated power) and power take-off (PTO) speed can be reduced [ 34]. This method improves engine ef ciency by maintaining high engine load and an engine speed at 60 80% of rated speed [ 35]. Signi cant improvements in fuel and tractive ef ciency from implementation of thismethod were achieved with two- and four-wheel drive tractors in Canada [ 69]. For maximum operating ef ciency, a tractor engine should be operated near its rated capacity.Many eld operations such as light tillage, planting, mechanical weed control, spraying, and hay-raking, how- ever, do not require full tractor power.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Sustainable agriculture energy|Electric tractors and farm machinery_qna_007
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the potential benefit of operating tractors at higher gears and lower engine speeds for lighter operations?
nodes.answer: Substantial fuel savings are possible by operating tractors at higher gears and lower engine speeds while maintaining the desired field speed for lighter operations.
nodes.paragraph: This is particularlytrue when older implements that were sized for smaller tractors are used with today S high-horsepower tractors or existing tractors are used in controlled traf C farming (CTF) and no-tillage operations, where power requirements are much lower. Many operations require xed ground speeds. For these lighter operations, substantial fuel sav-ings are possible by operating the tractor on a higher gear and lower engine speed, while maintaining the desired eld16 Agricultural Research (March 2025) 14(1):15 33 123 speed. The GUTB method will not suit all tractor opera- tions. Certain PTO operated implements require high engine speeds for the correct operation of the equipment and, as such, their use is incompatible with the GUTBmethod. When evaluating options for a new tractor pur- chase, it is recommended to clarify how energy ef ciency can be optimized for PTO applications and how the PTOaffects general engine ef ciency. The most basic ef ciency measure is to avoid overloading the engine by using a gear that is too high for the task. Adaptive driving depends on the operator receiving accurate feedback on both engine performance and driver performance.
